headNote: uncommitted working tree on the baseline; the parent commits
behaviorDelivered: Destroyed kept: the production outcome derivation (CampaignMatchHostOutcomeInbox.ts) commits every roster change as RosterUnitChanged 'repaired' carrying the unit's status, destroyed included; the fallback walk (reconcileCoopBattle.ts) does the same, so no combat outcome removes a unit.

The unit after the change: for a unit the host ledger holds, the outcome's payload is that ledger unit with the new status (its unitRef, unitSource and designation kept), so the reducer's replace does not drop fields a record checkpoint re-projects; an unknown unit is sent as {unitId, designation, status}. Added because rows o1 and o1c measured the journal and the live host disagreeing on exactly those fields after the host's save (diagnostic below); not named in the coordinator's list.

The hook: appendCampaignCombatOutcomeBatch takes an optional afterCommit and runs it on the transaction's handle after the receipt insert, in the committed arm only; the store's appendCombatOutcomeBatch passes this.rewriteRecordAfterCommand (installed by bindJournalCapabilityPorts on the co-op host's store). The flag constant line is untouched.

The rewrite (rewriteCampaignRecordAfterCommand, shared with command batches since U35e) also sets each roster projection unit's readiness from the journal's roster status (operational -> Ready, damaged -> Damaged, destroyed -> Destroyed) for units in both; force membership and every other field kept; journal-native gate unchanged.
The activity feed describes a 'repaired' change carrying status destroyed as '<designation> destroyed' under 'battle'.
The RosterUnitProjection readiness comment now says the saved record of a journal-native campaign takes readiness from the journal rewrite, so it can differ from the combat-state derivation.

nonClaims: No build and no Playwright; no browser: the host save is modelled by the live item route (a PUT at the held version, then a GET and a PUT of the server record), not by the persistence store or U35f refresh code.
The co-op host is driven directly over selectCampaignEventStore().store, not through a socket or ReconcileBattle frame.
recoveredUnit is out of scope (FN-u35d-recovered-unit-lost); a record without a roster projection gets no readiness patch; a journal unit absent from the projection is not added to the record.

The fallback walk (in-memory store, no inbox) still sends {unitId, designation, status}; it keeps a destroyed unit but does not carry the ledger unit fields forward (no checkpoint pairs with the in-memory store; not measured).
Rows t and a pin guard behaviour (t is red on the baseline only because no rewrite ran); they are not reproductions of a reported failure.
The wider gate suites ran with the constant false only; under the flip only the three row suites and U35e two suites were run.
No suite measures a command batch whose rewrite changes roster readiness (the shared rewrite now patches it; U35e suites stayed green).

findingsReportedNotFixed.finding: The outcome payload now spreads the ledger unit, which can carry sourceVersion; the campaign baseline schema pack's strict roster unit has no sourceVersion, so such a payload would be refused by that pack, as a genesis snapshot whose roster units carry sourceVersion already is (read, not run; the pack is not wired to production replay per its header).
A damaged unit's status change still reads '<designation> repaired' under 'technical' (pre-existing wording; the sentence names only destroyed).

The carry-forward of the ledger unit fields was not in the coordinator list; it was added because the o1/o1c agreement assertions (from U35d probe rows) measured the divergence. The parent may prefer to accept the rows without the agreement check instead.
The guest roster count includes destroyed units (already recorded as FN-u35g-kept-destroyed-units-in-guest-roster-count).

risksForTheParent: Authority: a first-receipt combat outcome on a journal-native campaign writes the saved record (version + 1, balance, date, roster readiness); a host save built before it answers 409 (rows o1, o1c, o2u).
Idempotency: a duplicate receipt appends nothing and leaves the stored row byte-identical (row i, M3).
Concurrency: the rewrite is inside the outcome transaction; a failing rewrite rolls back the consequences and the inbox receipt, and redelivery then commits once (row t, M2).
Migration: none; the rewrite spreads the raw stored JSON without the read migration ladder (as U35e).
Visible change: destroyed units stay in the journal, host state and mirrors with status destroyed; the feed reads '<designation> destroyed' (battle).
Lane B: authority, idempotency, concurrency and migration need the owner ruling on the merged head.
